memos.scout:
The honest case for buying is weak. The strongest point is the 30-minute return of +4.8% with a drawdown of only 0.14% from the 30-minute high, so the coin is holding its level. Recent volume is real: $1,986 over 15 minutes, with 57 buyers and 39 sellers, and net flow of +2.5 SOL shows buyers slightly outweighing sellers.

But the brief describes an operator-backed coin in its most concentrated form. Buyers ex-agent in the first two minutes were 17 wallets, with top-5 buyer share at 99.95% and bundle share at 100%. Roughly 940 SOL came in from almost nothing, and a launch bot was present. The last 15 minutes show 9.6 SOL bought against 7.1 SOL sold, and a 2.5 SOL net inflow is thin against a 1,040 SOL pool. Demand that is this concentrated can leave in one transaction, and the top holders have every incentive to exit once the flow fades.

Even at break-even base rates for operator coins, a $20 round trip costing 1.4-5.1% is a negative expectation. There is no case that real demand will persist for 30-60 minutes. I recommend skipping this coin.
memos.skeptic:
The most likely loss path is insider distribution by the operator. The first two minutes after graduation show 939.62 SOL bought from just 17 outside buyers, with top5_buyer_share at 0.9995 and bundle_share at 1.0, which fits the OPERATOR class: a concentrated group that accumulated before retail arrived. The curve shows top3_share of 1.0 and completer_share of 2.87, so a few wallets hold nearly everything.

The last 15 minutes reinforce this. Sellers (39) are outnumbering the 57 buyers, and sell_SOL of 7.07 against buy_SOL of 9.57 is a sell-heavy tape even though net_flow is positive. With the pool at 1,039.77 SOL and a market cap of $7.3M, one operator exit of a few hundred SOL would move price sharply, and a $20 ticket would be exposed to fees of 1.4-5.1% plus the 30-second execution lag. The flat 30-minute drawdown (0.14%) may reflect operator support rather than organic strength. I'd pass.
